Hello, and welcome

Come as you are. We will put the kettle on.

Dudhsagar Plantation is our family's farm: fifty green acres at the edge of Mollem National Park, a short drive from Dudhsagar Falls. There are five cottages, a spice garden, a forest trail and a swimming pool filled with natural water.

Mostly, though, there is time. Time for long breakfasts, slow walks and conversations that wander off somewhere nice. Stay a night or stay a week. Either way, you are very welcome here.

The natural pool

A swim the way nature intended

Our organic swimming pool is filled with living, natural water and kept clear without chlorine. It sits right in the garden, so you may share it with a dragonfly or two. They do not splash.

Soft on your skin

Natural water with nothing added. No stinging eyes, no chlorine hair.

Gentle on the land

Nothing harsh goes back into the soil that grows your breakfast.

Yours all day

Open to every guest, from the first quiet swim at sunrise to the last one before dinner.

Our story

It began with bare land and a stubborn dream

This was never meant to be a homestay. It was meant to be a farm that could look after itself. The guests came later, and we are so glad they did.

1984

No water, no power, no trees

Ajit Malkarnekar and his wife Doris began with barren land and one idea: bring the soil back to life, patiently and sustainably.

The next generation

Ashok comes home

Their son Ashok studied environmental economics in Germany, then came back to carry the same philosophy forward.

Today

Fifty acres that feed themselves

Fruit, spices, medicinal plants and cashew all grow here now, and the cashew becomes feni in our own still.

Gold for Sustainable Leadership, HomestaysOutlook Traveller Indian Responsible Tourism Awards 2025. We like to think the trees earned it.

Things to do

Plenty to do, and no pressure to do it

Some guests climb to waterfalls. Some never leave the veranda. Both are doing it exactly right.

On the farm

Neighbourhood trail

Seven unhurried kilometres through fields and villages and along the river. Wear shoes you like.

Birdwatching

More than 60 species live on the farm, with more in the sanctuary next door. Binoculars help. Patience helps more.

Natural farming

Get your hands in the soil the traditional way. It turned barren land into this garden, so it clearly works.

The spice tour

A guided walk to meet the spices from your kitchen shelf while they are still growing. A few will surprise you.

The heritage distillery

Watch cashew become feni and urak the old way: slowly, and over a wood fire.

A little further

Dudhsagar Waterfall

A bumpy jeep ride through the wildlife sanctuary, rewarded with a swim beneath the falls.

Tambdi Surla Temple and Waterfall

Goa's oldest temple, followed by a forest hike to a waterfall most visitors never find.

Saveri Waterfall and Usgalimol

A waterfall at Netravli and a riverbank of prehistoric rock carvings.

Salaulim Dam and Botanical Garden

A dam with a most unusual duck-bill spillway, and a garden to wander beside it.

Indo-Portuguese heritage homes

Step inside a grand Portuguese-era mansion at Chandor.

Spice tours Day out Camping All activities

By invitation, with Moving Arts Program

The Feni Trail

One day and one night on the farm with a small group. Follow the cashew from tree to copper still to glass, then stay for the river walk, an acoustic set by Elvis Lobo, a barbecue and a night walk to meet our glowing scorpions.

Sunday 29 to Monday 30 November

From our own still

Ouro, our spiced cashew feni

Grown here, distilled here and best enjoyed here. Our heritage distillery makes cashew feni and urak the traditional way, and Ouro is the one we are proudest of. Take a bottle home from the farm, or find it in select stores across Goa.

Meet Ouro De Goa
Planning your visit

When to come? Honestly, whenever.

The farm changes with the seasons, and each one has its own reasons to visit.

October to May

The dry season

  • Jeep safari to Dudhsagar Waterfall
  • Swims in the local river
  • Hikes through fields and villages
The monsoon

The green season

  • A hike to a secret waterfall
  • A natural fish spa
  • The farm at its most lush
A sample itinerary

The other side of Goa, in five days

Day 1Arrive, exhale, meet the farm

Check in, take the guided spice tour and visit the heritage distillery.

Day 2Dudhsagar Waterfall

A jeep safari to the falls (October to May), then the plantation nature trail.

Day 3Tambdi Surla

Visit Goa's oldest temple and hike to Tambdi falls.

Day 4Wild water

In the monsoon: hike to a secret waterfall, swim, and try a natural fish spa. In summer: swim in the local river and hike through fields and villages.

Day 5Heritage on the way out

Breakfast and checkout, then a visit to a Portuguese-era mansion.

Extra dayBecause five is never enough

Saveri Waterfall, Netravli Wildlife Sanctuary and the rock carvings at Rivona.

Room rates include breakfast and a plantation tour. Extra costs are mainly transport, entry fees and guiding. We are happy to tailor the plan to you. Activities depend on government restrictions at the time of travel.

Good to know

A few things guests often ask

Where exactly are you?

In Karmane village at the edge of Mollem National Park in South Goa, close to Dudhsagar Waterfall and the Bhagwan Mahaveer Wildlife Sanctuary. Far from the beach crowds, happily.

What is included in the room rate?

Breakfast and a plantation tour. Excursions cost extra, mainly for transport, entry fees and guiding.

What is an organic swimming pool?

A pool filled with natural water and kept clear without chlorine, set right inside the garden.

Can we visit just for the day?

Of course. We host spice tours, day outs and camping as well as farmstays. Call or message us and we will plan it together.

How do we join the Feni Trail?

It is by invitation and kept to a small group. Message Moving Arts Program on WhatsApp and they will tell you about the next one.
